Seahawks’ Week 1 win was bigger than the comeback: it may be an early test of QB depth in 2026

Seattle opened the season 1-0, but Sam Darnold’s early exit turned a narrow win into an immediate look at how much the Seahawks can absorb if the quarterback situation stays in flux.

By Seahawks Fan ZonePublished September 13, 20263 min readCategory: Analysis

The opener gave Seattle a win and a warning

The Seahawks got the result they wanted in their 2026 opener, beating their opponent 13-10 on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, to start the season 1-0. But the more important storyline for fans may be what happened along the way: Sam Darnold left early, and Seattle had to finish the game with Drew Lock. That makes this less a simple opening-night celebration than an early stress test for a team that may need answers at quarterback right away. [1] [2]

That matters because opening-week wins can hide as much as they reveal. Seattle was able to survive the loss of its starting quarterback in the first game of the year, but that only underscores how quickly the season can shift if the position remains unsettled. For fans, the encouraging part is the win; the concern is that the margin for error may already be thin. [1] [2]

What the team knows, and what it still does not

After the game, head coach Mike Macdonald said the team had ruled out a fracture and would do more testing on Darnold, but it was still too early to know whether he would be available for Week 2. That is the key verified update: there was good news on the most severe injury concern, but no firm prognosis yet. In other words, Seattle avoided the worst-case scenario without clearing the quarterback situation. [1]

NFL.com’s team page later reflected the same uncertainty more bluntly, listing Darnold as expected to miss Week 2 while noting he had avoided a major hip injury. It also showed the Seahawks at 1-0 and pointed to the next game at Arizona on Sept. 20, 2026. For a fan base trying to read the tea leaves, those details suggest the opener may have implications that stretch beyond one victory. [2]

Why this feels bigger than a standard comeback win

Seahawks.com framed the opener as a comeback built on resilience after Seattle erased a 10-point deficit and kept playing after Darnold exited early. That description is accurate, but the deeper lesson is about identity under pressure. This team has already shown it can handle disruption and still close out a game, which is a useful trait in any season and especially one that may demand immediate adjustment. [3]

At the same time, resilience is not a complete plan. If Darnold is unavailable or limited in Week 2, Seattle may need to lean more heavily on defense, situational football and quarterback contingency planning than it would prefer this early in the year. That is not a criticism of the opener; it is the practical takeaway from it. The Seahawks proved they can win a tight game with adversity. The bigger question is how often they can expect that formula to hold. [1] [2] [3]

What fans should watch next

The most meaningful development for Seahawks fans is not just that the team opened 1-0, but that the opener may already be defining how this season will need to be managed. If Darnold is back quickly, Seattle can treat Week 1 as a gritty one-off. If he is not, then the first game of 2026 becomes a preview of a season in which the Seahawks must win with flexibility rather than stability. [1] [2]

That is why the Week 1 result should be read in two ways at once: as a positive start, and as an early reminder that quarterback depth is not a theoretical issue. The Seahawks showed toughness, but they also revealed a potential pressure point. For fans, that combination makes the opener more informative than the final score alone. [1] [3]
